international.title: Democrats say Trump risked US security over Nvidia as Huang apologises | First Thing
international.summary: Reinstated CEO tells staff ‘I made some ‘terrible mistakes’, as questions remain over chips to China accusations. Plus a woman has an untimely encounter with some turkeys before Thanksgiving Good morning. Chuck Schumer has accused Jensen Huang , the newly reinstated Nvidia CEO, of shipping “extremely advanced chips to China” and violating US export control laws. On Tuesday, the senator said the move “amounts to the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the space race”, adding: “This is an unfathomable failure of enforcement by the Trump administration.” What did Huang say to Nvidia staff on his return? He apologised to staff and acknowledged he violated the code of conduct for having extramarital affairs, but pushed back on reports that Donald Trump was instrumental in his reinstatement as chief executive. “I made some terrible mistakes,” he said. “I was unfaithful to Lori, and I hurt my kids and, of course, I hurt all of you.” How has the market reacted now? Technology shares led a market retreat on Tuesday as caution returned after Huang’s extraordinary return to Nvidia days after he was forced to resign, with investors bracing for further volatility in a key sector driving economic growth worldwide. Live coverage here : Trump says pardon for Nvidia boss Huang “always an option” after accusations of breaking export laws. How close was her stunning result? Broderick prevailed by fewer than 400 votes, according to the Associated Press race call. DesJarlais, 62, who aligned himself closely with Trump during his time in office, conceded to Broderick last week after the razor-thin contest but the race was officially called on Tuesday.
